units: Sabb. VI, 5 (64ᵇ) שן תותבת ושן של זהב an inserted (natural) tooth or an (artificial) gold tooth; (Bab. ed. שן תותכת שן וכ׳, Ms. O. ושן, v. Rashi a. l.). Ib. 10, v. שׁוּעָל; a. fr.—Esp. (sub. נזק) the damage done by an animal’s eating.

<cite ref="Bava Kamma 2b:3">B. Kam. 2ᵇ</cite> <he>שלשה … הקרן והשן והרגל</he> three chief damages are mentioned (in the Scriptural text) with reference to the ox: damage by the horn, by the tooth, and by the foot.
<cite ref="Bava Kamma 2b:14">Ib.</cite> <he>שן יש הנאה וכ׳</he>, v. <cite ref="E00354"><he>הֶיזֵּק</he></cite>.

Ib. אשן ורגל it refers to damages by the tooth and by the foot; שן ורגל היכא כתיבי where is the damage by the tooth or the foot written (in the Biblical text)? Ib. ובער זו השן ubhiʿer (Ex. XXII, 4) this refers to damage by the tooth; a. fr.—Du. שִׁנַּיִים, שִׁנַּיִם, שִׁי׳.
<cite ref="Mishnah Chullin 1:2">Ḥull. I, 2</cite> <he>בכל … והש׳</he> you may cut ritually with anything, except … with teeth in the jaw.
<cite ref="Mishnah Chullin 1:2">Ib.</cite> <he>ואם החליקו שִׁינֶּיהָ</he> and if the teeth of the saw have been made smooth.
<cite ref="Mishnah Kelim 13:8">Kel. XIII, 8</cite> <he>שניטלו שִׁינָּיו</he> (a hackle) whose teeth are broken off.
<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 33">Gen. R. s. 33</cite> <he>חשש רבי את שיניו וכ׳</he> Rabbi suffered from tooth-ache for thirteen years.

<cite ref="Ketubot 111b:19">Keth. 111ᵇ</cite> <he>טוב המלבין ש׳ וכ׳</he> he who causes his neighbor to show the white of his teeth (who makes him cheerful) does better than he who gives him milk to drink.
Ib. א״ת לבן ש׳ אלא לבון ש׳ read not l’ben shinnayim (Gen. XLIX, 12) but libbun shinnayim (whitening of teeth, cheerfulness); a. fr.—2) any organ of the body resembling teeth, gland.—Du. as ab.

<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Yevamot 6:1:5">Y. Yeb. VI, beg. 7ᵇ</cite> <he>בית הש׳</he> that part of the vagina which has glands; <he>מבין הש׳ ולפנים</he> from the glands and farther inside; <cite ref="Niddah 41b">Nidd. 41ᵇ</cite>.
<cite ref="Chullin 16b:12">Ḥull. 16ᵇ</cite> <he>שיניו נושרות</he> the glands of his rectum will fall off; <cite ref="Shabbat 82a">Sabb. 82ᵃ</cite>; a. e.

<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 74:13">Gen. R. s. 74</cite> <he>כשן הזה של וכ׳</he> (the stone which Jacob put up was) as large as the peak of Tiberias; <cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Torah 130">Yalk. ib. 130</cite>; a. e.

Num. R. s. 312 (play on מי יג̇ור̇ … חזק כש̇ן̇ (ג̇ר̇ש̇ון̇ who can abide snow and hail, and cold and heat? He who is as strong as ivory (or marble?); אין שן אלא לשון חזק וכ׳ shen has the meaning of strong (ref. to Cant. V, 14); a. e
<cite ref="Shir HaShirim Rabbah 5:11">Cant. R. to V, 11</cite>; <cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Nach 991:4">Yalk. ib. 991</cite>, v. <cite ref="P01518"><he>עֶשֶׁת</he></cite>.
